lines.say: Two mothers die for every hundred thousand births. That is the lowest on this chart. Which country is it?
Maternal deaths per hundred thousand live births, since 1990. Lowest first.
In 1990, Egypt and Iran lose a hundred and seven.
Britain leads with six. America, twelve. Israel, twenty nine.
Then the region falls fast. Egypt ends at seventeen.
Turkey, from forty two to fifteen. Lebanon and Iran end at fifteen and sixteen.
America goes the other way. Twelve, then seventeen.
2021, the pandemic, spikes almost everywhere. Jordan hits seventy nine.
Saudi Arabia ends at seven. Germany, four. The UAE, three.
Why did America go backwards? Tell me in the comments.
And the lowest on the chart?

end.balance: Modelled UN estimates. Small numbers *swing yearly.*

caption_en:
In 1990 this country was eighth of twelve. Guess where it finished.

Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births, 2023 (UN modelled estimates via the World Bank):
Israel 2
UAE 3
Germany 4
Saudi Arabia 7
UK 8
Turkey 15
Lebanon 15
Iran 16
Egypt 17
USA 17
Syria 20
Jordan 31

1990: UK 6, USA 12, Israel 29, Egypt 107, Iran 107. The USA rose from 12 to 17 (31 in 2021). The pandemic year 2021 spiked almost everywhere (Jordan 79, Lebanon 54, Iran 51).
These are modelled estimates; small numbers move from year to year.

Source: WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, World Bank Group and UNDESA (MMEIG) via World Bank, World Development Indicators, SH.STA.MMRT, 1990 to 2023. The animation interpolates between years.
Photos: Tel Aviv University medical building (Zalmanson Zeller, PikiWiki, CC BY 2.5), Riyadh (B.alotaby, CC BY-SA 4.0), Soroka and Ben Gurion University (Omer Berner, CC BY-SA 4.0), via Wikimedia Commons.
Made with AI tools. AI voice (Noam's own cloned voice).
